findings.title: Closed polylines are flattened without a planarity check
findings.body: Closed PolyLines are converted to XY segments and assigned their average Z without verifying that their vertices lie on a horizontal plane. The loose-line path explicitly rejects non-horizontal lines, but this path can accept a 3D polyline whose XY projection is rectangular and place a foundation at an invented average elevation. Reject loops whose Z range exceeds the elevation tolerance before extracting their projected face.

findings.title: Closure tolerance is incompatible with polygonization tolerance
findings.body: A PolyLine is classified as closed when its endpoints are less than 0.01 feet apart, but ExtractFromSegments uses a PlanarFaceExtractor tolerance of 0.001 feet and no explicit segment is added from the last point to the first. Consequently, endpoint gaps between 0.001 and 0.01 feet enter the closed-loop path but may not form a face, silently omitting a foundation. Append an explicit closing segment or use a consistent snapping/closure tolerance.

findings.title: Rotation behavior is not meaningfully tested
findings.body: The test uses an axis-aligned rectangle and expects a zero angle. It would still pass if rotation extraction were hard-coded to zero or broken for rotated CAD geometry. Since foundation orientation is part of the asserted extraction contract and affects automatic placement, add a non-axis-aligned rectangle with a known angle and verify its dimensions, center, and rotation.
